case.name: Fictional North Quay help desk
case.brief: A 12-person help desk handles 60 handbook questions each week. Its lead wants a pilot to test whether staff can find a supported answer faster. Current answer time and error rate have never been measured. The pilot has ten working days and no permission to use employee records.
rules: Remote work is allowed up to two days each week with manager approval.
Expense receipts must be submitted within 30 days.
questions: May I work remotely for two days with manager approval?
When must I submit a receipt?
What is the allowance for travel meals?

account-manager.attempt: Write three discovery questions that distinguish a search problem from a staffing problem. Name the buyer and the cheapest test of demand.
account-manager.acceptance: A buyer could decline the pilot based on the stated success threshold.
account-manager.transfer: The budget owner freezes new software purchases. Revise the next ask.

solution-engineer.attempt: Specify the smallest repeatable demonstration, a manual baseline and two failure cases.
solution-engineer.acceptance: A colleague can reproduce the baseline and reject the pilot using the same measure.
solution-engineer.transfer: The sponsor now requires every answer in under two seconds on a laptop with no network. Replace an online dependency or document how the pilot will test latency offline.

ai-architect.attempt: Compare two viable designs for data access, an evaluation boundary and a reversible rollout.
ai-architect.acceptance: Trace one request from source to answer, name the data owner and record a rollback trigger.
ai-architect.transfer: One source loses its access approval. Revisit scope, cost and the chosen design.

technical-consultant.attempt: Write the decision, deliverables, exclusions, acceptance owner and handover for a small engagement.
technical-consultant.acceptance: A client and delivery lead can identify the same acceptance event and who owns remediation.
technical-consultant.transfer: The client halves the delivery window. Negotiate one explicit scope cut.

student.attempt: Using paper or a text editor, compare three sample questions to the two handbook rules. Record the source or mark the answer unknown.
student.acceptance: For each answer, a peer can trace the exact rule or identify the missing fact.
student.transfer: The remote-work rule changes to one day. Identify which answer changes and cite the new rule.

stages.start: Draft your first attempt using only the fictional brief. Record each assumption and leave unknowns visible.
stages.draft: Critique the existing draft against the acceptance condition. Record one defect, the change made and the revised artifact.
stages.revised: Apply the changed constraint to the revised artifact. Preserve the earlier decision and explain what now changes.
